claims.text: Sliding-induced mechanical deformation forms an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer in CoCrFeMnNi.
The near-surface refinement is associated with dynamic amorphization under mechanical stress.
The dynamically formed ultra-nanocrystalline layer is associated with low friction and wear.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer rapidly oxidizes in a corrosive environment.
Oxidation of the ultra-nanocrystalline layer forms a protective passivation film.
Nanocrystalline material has a high density of reactive sites that accelerates oxidation.
The nanocrystalline structure promotes rapid and uniform oxide passivation.
The passivating oxide film suppresses further mechanical wear.
The passivating oxide film limits aggressive metal dissolution by electrochemically stabilizing the surface.
A single-phase CoCrFeMnNi alloy can have an initially coarse-grained state.
The proposed initial alloy has minimal pre-existing oxide.
Oxidation and mixed-metal oxide-film formation are suppressed or mitigated in an inert environment.
Compared with an inert-environment or no-nanocrystallization baseline, an oxidizing environment will reduce total tribo-corrosion material loss.
Compared with the baseline, rapid passivation will attenuate the wear component of degradation.
Compared with the baseline, rapid passivation will attenuate the corrosion component of degradation.
The protective mechanism requires sufficient oxygen and electrochemical potential for oxidation.
The mechanism will become ineffective under highly reducing conditions or when low temperature or low oxidant concentration makes oxidation too slow.

contradictions.description: The mediator is attributed to mechanical deformation during wear, which occurs in both test environments, but the baseline and falsification design partly treat the inert condition as though it should lack a comparable nanocrystalline layer. The cited evidence specifically reports formation of that layer under inert ultra-high-vacuum conditions.

The baseline alternates between two non-equivalent comparators: an alloy lacking dynamic nanocrystallization and an alloy tested in an inert environment. The cited inert-environment system does undergo dynamic nanocrystallization and already exhibits exceptionally low wear, so the predicted comparison is not internally well-defined.
